Applicable aspects: L01 motivates the question but its toroidal proposal does not supply a reproduced self-confinement evolution. Sebens interprets a Dirac field, rather than replacing it by Maxwell light. The inspected L07 v1 is titled *Electromagnetic Field from the Skyrme Term*. The arXiv history identifies [v4](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/0207167v4) with the registered journal title. Fresh v4 Section II, Eqs. (11)–(20), shows additional internal-field dynamics, an elementary-charge-dependent coupling and a dimensional potential parameter; these must be distinguished from derived predictions.

Impact: no electromagnetic-wave electron conclusion follows. Keep charge, angular momentum, spin/statistics and scale-setting tests separate. Use the verified v4 mapping before importing equations; do not transfer its elementary-charge constant into the baseline as an emergent prediction.

## A08 — Experimental magnetic-moment benchmark

Source: Fan et al., [author-hosted published PRL PDF](https://cfp.physics.northwestern.edu/documents/2023MeasurementElectronMangeticMoment.pdf), fresh inspection of first page, Eqs. (1)–(3) and stated uncertainty.

Applicable aspect: the measured $g/2$ is extracted from spin, cyclotron and anomaly-frequency ratios with a quantified uncertainty. This is a future independent benchmark, not a current simulation target fitted by choosing a length or amplitude.

Impact: retain L08 and S7's separate quantum-analysis gate. A classical circulation giving an approximate gyromagnetic ratio does not reproduce the stated measurement or establish Fermi statistics. No claim that this remains the newest measurement is made by the backward-reference search.

## A09 — Nonlinear terms and numerical-method references

L16–L17's previously inspected invariant-based null-background argument remains relevant: adding a named nonlinear action does not imply its selected null background changes. The present checkpoint retrieves the versioned PDFs but does not claim a fresh complete derivation of each variation. L03/L10 likewise retain their existing source-specific model mappings; their accessible PDFs are not new independent numerical reproductions. L18 remains an absorbing-layer method reference; the retrieved publisher material is abstract/reference-level and is not enough to implement PML.

Impact: MOD-002 and BND-001 remain required. No change to the existing propagator or dependency lock is justified at this point. Open-boundary numerical experiments require an independent equation-level design and reflection/loss validation.

## Remaining second-pass workload

All other retained corpus items still require paper-specific notes at the appropriate review depth. Candidate topics include primary helicity/linking definitions, null congruences, line-transport criteria, knot invariants, absorbing boundaries, and spin/statistics quantisation. The staged ledger must identify the precise retained set before this checklist can be marked complete. AI assistance: Codex drafted these targeted notes; source reading is not independent expert certification.

# Provisional impact assessment of S1–S4-A

This is an **initial audit**, not the completed assessment requested after both literature passes. It compares the merged baseline `ae0a190` with the targeted inspections in [the second-pass notes](SECOND-PASS.md). Most corpus records still lack substantive content review. A completed collector or a passing integrity check cannot close that gap.
